shadow:
Some yeses cost nothing on the outside and a great deal on the inside. You agree to the smaller version of the day. You take the job that pays but does not pull at you. You let the dream go quiet, not in one decision but in a thousand of them, each one too small to argue with.

This is compromise, and most people read it as being sensible. That is the misread. Being sensible is choosing the steady thing for a reason you can stand behind. Compromise is choosing the steady thing because you have stopped believing the other thing was ever yours to reach.

It has a feel to it. A small shrinking, somewhere under the ribs, every time you trade the true answer for the easier one. You can learn to stop noticing that shrinking. Plenty of people do.

But notice this. The thing that shrinks is still in there. It did not leave. It is the same fire that wants the bigger life, only banked low and waiting. The shrinking is not the absence of your dream. It is the dream telling you it is still alive, in the only voice it has left.
repressive: Some people answer the shrinking by calling it humility. They want little, ask for little, tell themselves wanting more was always a kind of vanity. It looks like contentment. The fire has just been turned down so far they cannot hear it.
reactive: Others answer it by working harder at the wrong thing. They pour everything into proving they matter, chasing the recognition that will finally settle it. The recognition arrives. It does not settle anything, because it was never the hunger underneath.
gift:
A person stops trading the true answer away, and something inside shifts. Not all at once. One uncompromised choice, then another, small enough that the world barely registers them. But the fire under the ribs feels them, and it starts to climb.

What climbs is competence. Not skill, though skill comes into it. Competence is what happens to the work of someone who has stopped being at war with their own day. They do the thing well because they actually want the thing, and wanting it does something to the doing.

There is a way of pulling a saw toward your belly instead of pushing it away. The cut comes out finer and your arm is not tired. Competence works like that. It finds the short way through because it is paying close attention, and it is paying close attention because it cares.

This is also why it spreads. Put one person who loves their work into a small room of people and watch what happens to the room. The caring is catching. And the fire, once it is properly lit and fed, does not want to warm only the one who lit it. It starts reaching for what else it could warm.
siddhi:
By this point the fire is not something a person tends. It is what they are made of. There is no hoarding left, no careful accounting of what went out against what came back. There is just giving, the way the sun gives, with no idea of return and no need for one.

This is bounteousness. The wealth of it is not in what is held but in what keeps moving through. A life like this generates. Love, luck, the right people arriving at the right hour, all of it pulled in and passed on, because a thing that radiates cannot help drawing more of itself toward the warmth.

It runs on gratitude, this far up. Not gratitude as a practice. Gratitude as the plain fact of being amazed that there was ever a spark at all. From here you can look back at the long compromised years, the shrinking, the dream kept barely lit. None of it was the failure it felt like. It was the wood. It was what the fire was always going to burn.
